title: The affine line
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it. Let $V$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. For $E$ use its continuous-function condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; for $\Qlb$ use the condensed ring of continuous functions with values in some finite subextension [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. The coefficient ring on a scheme $X$ is its pullback $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\underline\Lambda$ from the point [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $p:\mathbf A^1_V\to V$ be the affine-line projection [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], $j:\mathbf A^1_V\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_V$ the standard open immersion, and $q:\mathbf P^1_V\to V$ the projective-line projection [def-nagata-relative-projective-space], so $p=q\circ j$.

Use the ambient module-object derived categories and derived pullbacks of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], bounded constructible complexes $\Dbc$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and localizing closure as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The functor $Rp_!$ is the compactification functor of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek], and $p^!$ is its right adjoint on the localizing closures from [sk-prop-sf-existence]. Write $K(1)=K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}\Lambda_X(1)$ for the Tate twist of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist], and $[2]$ for cohomological shift. Then:

1. $j_!$ and $j^*$ preserve the respective categories $\Loc(\Dbc(-,\Lambda))$, and their restrictions satisfy $j_!\dashv j^*$;
2. $Rp_!\simeq Rq_*\circ j_!$ on these categories;
3. $Rp_!$ is left adjoint to $p^*(1)[2]$, and there is a natural isomorphism
$$
p^!\simeq p^*(1)[2]:\Loc(\Dbc(V,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dbc(\mathbf A^1_V,\Lambda)),
$$
uniquely determined by compatibility with the two adjunction counits.

proof.text: The standard-chart theorem [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] gives the open immersion $j$ over $V$, hence $qj=p$. By [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], the projective line has the finite homogeneous-coordinate set $\{0,1\}$. Apply [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] to that set and $S=V$: $q$ is proper. These are the same standard chart and proper projection as in the original compactification argument.

source.place: Proof (2): standard chart and proper projective-line projection.

proof.text: For every affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset V$, [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] identifies $p^{-1}(W)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$. Therefore $p$ is affine by the definition [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. The single algebra generator $t$ gives a one-member affine cover of each preimage by a finitely generated $R$-algebra; by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $p$ is locally of finite type (indeed finite type). This is only the defining polynomial-chart calculation; no separatedness assertion is inferred from it.

source.place: Tag 01M0 (definition-affine-n-space), following affine-chart description; morphisms.tex Tags 01S6 (definition-affine) and 01T1 (definition-finite-type).

proof.text: Apply clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] to the affine map $p$ of step 2: it is quasi-compact and separated. The properness of $q$ in step 1, unpacked by [def-weil-proper-morphism], makes $q$ separated and of finite type, hence quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $V$ is separated of finite type over the field $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes $V$ qcqs. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied separately to the quasi-compact maps $p,q$ with quasi-compact target $V$, now makes both $\mathbf A^1_V$ and $\mathbf P^1_V$ quasi-compact.

source.place: Tags 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated), 01W1 (definition-proper); schemes.tex Tag 01K4 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine) and lemma-composition-quasi-compact, via the cited permanence nodes.

proof.text: Write $a:V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure map. For $r=p$ and $r=q$, both $r$ and $a$ are separated and locally of finite type by the preceding steps and the hypotheses on $V$. Clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] gives the same two properties for $ar$. The target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The source of $ar$ is quasi-compact by step 3, so clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes $ar$ quasi-compact. Thus $ar$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Both total spaces are separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] makes them qcqs. Their structure maps are $ap,aq$, and $qj=p$ ensures that all maps used here are $k$-morphisms.

source.place: Tags 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence, composition), 03GI (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence), 01K4 (lemma-quasi-compact-affine); morphisms.tex Tag 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type), through clause (e) of the cited node.

proof.text: The source $\mathbf A^1_V$ is quasi-compact and the target $\mathbf P^1_V$ is quasi-separated by steps 3–4. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] therefore proves that $j$ is quasi-compact. Together with its open-immersion property, properness of $q$, and $qj=p$ from step 1, this is precisely a compactification $c=(j,q)$ under [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. Thus all the geometry required below has been verified by cited statements, including the standing setting and qcqs hypotheses.

source.place: Proof (2): finish the standard compactification, using Stacks Tag 03GI as stated by the cited permanence node instead of an inline principal-open argument.

proof.text: For $X=V,\mathbf A^1_V,\mathbf P^1_V$, apply [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] to the qcqs scheme $X$ and $\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, obtaining $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)=\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and equality of their localizing closures. Clause 1 of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction], with the quasi-compact open $j$ and qcqs target verified in steps 1–5, gives functors $j_!$ and $j^*$ between the corresponding $\Loc(\Dctf)$ categories and $j_!\dashv j^*$. Replacing these full subcategories by the equal $\Loc(\Dbc)$ subcategories proves (1). Only clause 1 of that node is used.

source.place: Proof (1): preservation and restricted open adjunction, using the existing stronger open-immersion statement.

proof.text: For the compactification $c=(j,q)$ of step 5, the definition [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] gives $Rp_!^c=Rq_*D(j_!)$. The functor of [sk-prop-sf-existence] is defined using a chosen compactification $c_p$. Apply [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] to $p$, $c_p$ and $c$; $p$ is separated of finite type and its target $V$ is qcqs, as checked in steps 1–4. It gives a natural isomorphism $Rp_!^{c_p}\simeq Rp_!^c$ on $\Loc(\Dctf)$. The equalities of categories in step 6 give $Rp_!\simeq Rq_*j_!$ on the claimed $\Loc(\Dbc)$ categories, proving (2). Here $j_!$ denotes its exact levelwise derived functor.

source.place: Proof (2): definition for the standard compactification and comparison with the chosen one.

proof.text: Identify the candidate right adjoint. The composition isomorphism of module pullbacks in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] gives $j^*q^*\simeq(qj)^*=p^*$ on sheaves. These pullbacks are exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], so their derived versions in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] are computed levelwise. Applying the sheaf composition isomorphism in every degree therefore gives the same natural isomorphism on arbitrary unbounded complexes, and then on their localizing subcategories. An exact levelwise pullback commutes with cohomological shifts: both complexes in degree $n$ have term $j^*(L^{n+2})$ and differential $j^*(d^{n+2})$. Apply the final assertion of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] with $f=j$ and $K=q^*N$; $\ell$ is invertible since $p\ne\ell$. It gives $j^*((q^*N)(1))\simeq(j^*q^*N)(1)$. Combining these natural identifications yields $j^*(q^*N(1)[2])\simeq p^*N(1)[2]$ for every $N\in\Loc(\Dbc(V,\Lambda))$.

source.place: Proof (3): the identity $j^*q^*(1)[2]=p^*(1)[2]$, with coefficient category, twist and shift checked.

proof.text:
Use the adjunction $Rq_*\dashv q^*(1)[2]$ explicitly asserted by [det-prop-p1-adjunction-rational-triangle], applied over $Y=V$ with the same rational coefficient $\Lambda$. For $M\in\Loc(\Dbc(\mathbf A^1_V,\Lambda))$ and $N\in\Loc(\Dbc(V,\Lambda))$, steps 6–8 give
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(Rp_!M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rq_*j_!M,N)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(j_!M,q^*N(1)[2])\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,j^*(q^*N(1)[2]))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(M,p^*N(1)[2]).
$$
Every bijection is natural in $M,N$: the first and last are induced by the natural isomorphisms of steps 7 and 8, and the middle two are the Hom bijections of the projective-line and open adjunctions. Their inverses in reverse order give the inverse composite. This exhibits $Rp_!\dashv p^*(1)[2]$, including that the displayed right adjoint takes values in the required localizing category.

source.place: Proof (3): compose the two adjunctions through their natural Hom bijections.

proof.text: By [sk-prop-sf-existence], $p^!$ is a right adjoint of this same $Rp_!$ on $\Loc(\Dctf)$, hence on the equal $\Loc(\Dbc)$ categories of step 6. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to $F=Rp_!$, $G=p^!$ and $J=p^*(1)[2]$, the latter adjunction being step 9. The $J$-transpose of the counit $Rp_!p^!N\to N$ gives the component $p^!N\to p^*N(1)[2]$; the cited statement makes these components natural, invertible and uniquely compatible with the counits. This proves the final assertion of (3).

source.place: Proof (3), final sentence: uniqueness of right adjoints and counit compatibility.

lean.statement: theorem det_cor_affine_space_rational_line (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Fact (ringChar k).Prime] [Fact (ringChar k ≠ ℓ)] (V : Scheme.{u}) [V.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (V ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (V ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (V ↘ Spec (.of k))] : (∀ E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ, affineLineRationalAssertion (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E.1) V (affineLineChosenCompactification k V) (fun X ↦ rationalTwistFunctor (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E.1) X (spRationalTwist X ℓ E))) ∧ affineLineRationalAssertion (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) V (affineLineChosenCompactification k V) (fun X ↦ rationalTwistFunctor (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj ℓ) X (spQbarTwist X ℓ))
lean.note: The assertion specializes the recorded generic localizing closure to constantModelBoundedConstructible (Dbc), uses the published Nagata compactificationOverField of the affine projection in Over(Spec k), and characterizes restrictions by ambient natural isomorphisms. The uniqueness clause applies to every right adjoint of this same restricted compact-support functor, hence to the exceptional adjoint. The projective line and standard chart use the base-change model explicitly specified by the node proof and its chart dependency blueprint_update.
